ending: Aunt Josephine, who had gone into hiding to fake her own death, is discovered by the children in Curdled Cave, but her fearfulness dooms her: crossing Lake Lachrymose during Hurricane Herman, the boat is swarmed by the deadly Lachrymose Leeches, and Captain Sham forces the terrified Josephine overboard, where she is killed. Back on shore the Baudelaires expose Captain Sham as Count Olaf by revealing the eye tattoo hidden beneath his fake peg leg, but before Mr. Poe and the others can seize him, Olaf escapes once more. The children have lost another guardian, and their fortune remains the prize Olaf is determined to claim. Mr. Poe takes the orphans back into his care to place them somewhere new, while Count Olaf, exposed but uncaught, slips away to plan his next disguise and his next attempt on the Baudelaires and their money.
in_short: The Baudelaires are sent to live with fearful, grammar-obsessed Aunt Josephine, whose house teeters on stilts over Lake Lachrymose. In town they meet Captain Sham, a peg-legged sailor they recognize as Count Olaf in disguise, who charms the timid Josephine. Soon Josephine seems to throw herself out her great window into the lake, leaving a note naming Captain Sham as the children's new guardian. Noticing that the note is full of grammatical errors unthinkable for Josephine, the children decode them as a secret message and realize she is alive and hiding in Curdled Cave. During Hurricane Herman they sail across the leech-infested lake and find her, but on the way back the Lachrymose Leeches attack, and Captain Sham forces Josephine into the water to be devoured. On shore the children expose Sham as Olaf by revealing his ankle tattoo, but he escapes yet again. Aunt Josephine is dead, and the orphans are returned to Mr. Poe.

recaps.text: After a fire killed their parents, the Baudelaire orphans, inventor Violet, reader Klaus, and biting baby Sunny, inherited a fortune held in trust and were placed by the banker Mr. Poe with the cruel actor Count Olaf. Olaf tried to steal the money by forcing Violet into a fake marriage, then escaped when she foiled him. The children were next sent to their kind Uncle Monty, a herpetologist, but Olaf followed in disguise as an assistant named Stephano, murdered Monty, and nearly abducted them before the children exposed him; again he escaped, marked always by his single eyebrow and the eye tattooed on his ankle. Having lost two guardians and survived Olaf twice, the orphans are placed by Mr. Poe with yet another relative, fearing that Olaf will appear once more in some new false identity to pursue them and their inheritance.

Mr. Poe delivers the Baudelaires to Aunt Josephine, a nervous widow whose house sits on stilts high over Lake Lachrymose. Josephine is fanatical about correct grammar and terrified of an endless list of ordinary things, from the stove to doorknobs, so her home is cold and comfortless. On a trip into town for groceries the children meet Captain Sham, a sailor with an eye patch and a wooden peg leg who rents out sailboats. Despite his eagerness to befriend Josephine, the children recognize him as Count Olaf in disguise and are alarmed to see him worming his way into their fearful guardian's good graces. They try to warn Josephine and Mr. Poe, but the adults dismiss their suspicions, and the orphans realize that danger has once again followed them to their new home over the water.

Captain Sham continues to charm the anxious Aunt Josephine while the children's warnings go unheeded. Then disaster strikes: Josephine's great window is found shattered, and she appears to have thrown herself out into the lake below, leaving behind a note that makes Captain Sham the children's new guardian. The Baudelaires are grief-stricken but immediately suspicious, because the note is riddled with grammatical mistakes that the grammar-obsessed Josephine would never have made. Studying it closely, they conclude that the errors are deliberate, a hidden message left for them, and that their aunt may not be dead at all. As Captain Sham prepares to take custody of them, the children race to decode the note before they can be handed over to the man they know to be Count Olaf.

The children decipher the intentional errors in the note and discover that Aunt Josephine has faked her death and is hiding in Curdled Cave across Lake Lachrymose. With Hurricane Herman bearing down, they take a sailboat out onto the storm-tossed water, braving wind, waves, and the dreaded Lachrymose Leeches that live in the lake, and reach the cave. There they find Josephine alive but paralyzed by her fears, reluctant to leave her hiding place or to face Captain Sham. The Baudelaires persuade her to come with them, hoping to return safely and expose Sham as Count Olaf, but the crossing back across the churning lake will be far more dangerous than the journey out.

On the return voyage the Lachrymose Leeches, drawn by the fact that Josephine has recently eaten, swarm and attack the boat. Captain Sham appears in his own vessel, and rather than rescue Josephine he forces her into the water, where the leeches devour her. Back on shore, Sham tries to claim the children and their fortune, but the Baudelaires expose him as Count Olaf by revealing the eye tattoo hidden beneath his false peg leg. Confronted at last, Olaf escapes yet again before Mr. Poe can have him arrested, vanishing to plan his next scheme. Aunt Josephine, undone by her own fearfulness, is dead, and the orphans, having lost a third guardian, are returned to Mr. Poe's care to be placed somewhere new while Count Olaf remains free.
